title: Tidal Bridge Performance Scouting Session
summary: Introductory partner call to map Tidal Bridge's hybrid GPU needs to Redwood's dedicated/private offerings. Main themes: latency targets for inference (<60ms p50 for 512 tokens), cost tradeoffs, on-prem VPC requirements, SSO/KMS compliance, and a short pilot to validate perf and integration patterns.
action_items: Jordan Kim: Share pilot scope doc + pricing spreadsheet by 2029-05-16
Priya Rao: Prepare a short benchmark plan + sample workload template by 2029-05-17
Aisha Rahman (Tidal Bridge): Send SOC2 report and required compliance checklist by 2029-05-15
next_steps: Schedule a 90-min pilot kickoff (Redwood SE + Tidal Bridge infra) week of 2029-05-20
Redwood to run a 48-hour baseline benchmark on a 4xA100 config and share results
Tidal Bridge to provide a sanitized sample workload and expected traffic pattern
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2029-05-13 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood Solutions), Marco Silva (Tidal Bridge CTO), Dana Ortiz (Platform Eng), Liu Chen (Procurement), Aisha Rahman (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Intro, scoping, security, pilot and next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for making the time. i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE here. real quick can folks introduce themselves?
[00:12] Marco Silva: Marco Silva, CTO at Tidal Bridge. we do real-time maritime risk scoring, so latency is like, pretty important for us.
[00:20] Dana Ortiz: Dana, platform eng - we manage the kubes and the on-prem infra.
[00:26] Liu Chen: Liu, procurement - i'll be looped in on contracts.
[00:29] Aisha Rahman: Aisha, security - will be driving compliance checks.
[00:33] Priya Rao: Priya, SE at Redwood - i'll be the technical lead for the pilot.
[00:37] Evan Park: Evan from solutions - i'll help map our offering to your cost goals.

[00:45] Jordan Kim: Great. Purpose today is a quick partner scouting — to see fit between Tidal Bridge's latency/cost constraints and our Dedicated/Private options, and to outline a lightweight pilot. we also want to flag any security blockers early.
[01:02] Marco Silva: yeah, so our numbers: typical request is around 400-600 tokens, tail is up to 1k. p50 we wanna be under 60ms, p95 under 220ms. throughput is spikey — we have bursts when a vessel crosses a geofence.
[01:22] Priya Rao: okay, that's helpful. couple clarifying q's — is that end-to-end including network? or just inference server time?
[01:29] Marco Silva: that's server-side inference only, we control the network in our edge POPs.
[01:34] Dana Ortiz: we run a mix of cloud and on-prem GPUs; for regulated customers we keep inference on prem in our DCs — isolated racks.
[01:44] Jordan Kim: got it. sounds like Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem package) might be a match — you can run our control plane in your VPC and options for air-gapped on-prem too. quick note, sometimes our product name shows as Redwood dedicate in transcripts - ignore that, it's the Dedicated/Private family.
[02:05] Marco Silva: two big questions: 1) can you hit that 60ms p50 for ~512 tokens on our on-prem racks? and 2) what's the cost delta vs hosted?
[02:16] Priya Rao: for 512 tokens on modern A100-class hardware with our optimized runtime and kv caching, p50 at 60ms is achievable but depends on batching and quantization. if you need strict p50 we may recommend smaller batch windows and a dedicated pool. cost-wise dedicated reserved capacity will be higher than hosted on a pure $/token basis, but predictable and with lower tail latency.
[02:41] Evan Park: putting numbers on that in a pilot is the best. a small reserved pool — like 4 GPUs — for the test will let us measure real traffic and tune batching, prewarm kv caches, and try int8 quantization to reduce cost.
[02:57] Dana Ortiz: on the on-prem side, we have Pelican racks with 8xA40 per cage, but our network to the edge POPs has some NAT layers. will that be an issue?
[03:08] Priya Rao: NAT is fine as long as we can reach the control plane endpoints or run the control plane inside your VPC. the more friction is audit logs and key management — if you need KMS/HSM for model keys that's supported but requires early planning.
[03:23] Aisha Rahman: we need SOC2 type II evidence, ISO attestation, and also a pointer to how audit logs are stored and for how long. is that in your security pack?
[03:32] Jordan Kim: yes, we'll send the security pack. we have SOC2 and ISO docs, and options for longer retention or forwarding logs to your SIEM. we'll also include an architecture note on how audit events look.
[03:42] Marco Silva: how about network egress/data residency — we can't send raw sensor data off-prem for certain customers. can you run inference entirely inside our VPC?
[03:50] Priya Rao: yes, Redwood Private can run the control plane in your VPC and the runtime nodes stay within your network. for air-gapped we do an on-prem package but it's a longer install.
[04:01] Marco Silva: good. next, about models — we primarily want to use an open LLM tuned for shorter responses, and want to try a smaller 7B variant in prod for cost. you support model catalog and quantization recommendations?
[04:11] Evan Park: yep, we maintain a curated catalog. Optimize can recommend quant profiles and batch settings per workload. one caveat — a 7B quantized model may have slightly different hallucination characteristics; we tie regressions to prompt sets in our evals.
[04:24] Dana Ortiz: any constraints on sequence length or kv-cache behavior we should know?
[04:28] Priya Rao: kv cache scales with sequence length and memory, but our runtime does dynamic kv eviction and continuous batching. for long session state you may need larger GPU memory or dedicate L2 cache nodes.
[04:39] Marco Silva: sample workload — we have 80% of requests ~512 tokens, 15% under 128 tokens, 5% over 1k. burst qps about 600 for a few secs.
[04:51] Priya Rao: that burst pattern suggests autoscaling and burst capacity are important — Dedicated pools can be configured with burst nodes. for strict latency we can tune batch windows and enable prefix caching.
[05:03] Jordan Kim: procurement question — Liu, any timeline constraints or contracting process we should align with?
[05:08] Liu Chen: we have Q3 budget and want pilot in May-June. procurement will evaluate pricing and T&Cs; we may push for term commitments if cost is favorable.
[05:16] Marco Silva: security will be a gating factor. Aisha, what's your high bar?
[05:19] Aisha Rahman: basically SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration, encryption at-rest, and an ability to review logs. if Redwood can support an on-prem control plane and provide attestation that no telemetry leaves our boundary, that's ideal.
[05:33] Priya Rao: all doable — we'll include options for encryption and for forwarding logs to your SIEM. note that some telemetry like runtime health checks can be suppressed in air-gapped installs.
[05:43] Marco Silva: great. can you talk briefly about monitoring and debugging? we need request-level traces and token-level cost breakdowns for debugging and billing.
[05:52] Evan Park: our console provides token-level cost, latency heatmaps per model/route, and trace IDs you can export to your tracing system. for private installs, we can forward traces into your tracing backend.
[06:05] Dana Ortiz: what's the support SLA for Dedicated/private? we run 24/7 critical flows.
[06:09] Jordan Kim: we offer enterprise SLAs with 4-hour response for P1 and optional 24/7 pager for critical incidents in higher tiers. SLA details we'll include in the contract doc.
[06:18] Marco Silva: what's the expected work to onboard an on-prem cluster? ballpark hours for SE+ops?
[06:22] Priya Rao: for a standard Private deploy in your DC, typical lift for a pilot is ~2-3 weeks including config, network, and security review, less if you already have an orchestrator and NFS. air-gapped is longer — 4-6 weeks.
[06:36] Marco Silva: ok. one technical ask — we want to run a pilot with our anonymized traffic that mimics bursts; can you do a bench with 4 GPUs and simulate our pattern?
[06:46] Priya Rao: yes. our plan: 1) you share sanitized workload + qps curve; 2) we stand up a 4-GPU test pool (A100/A40 depending on your infra), 3) run a 48-hour test with kv cache warmups and spike windows, 4) produce a perf/cost report.
[07:03] Evan Park: we'll also try int8 quantization and a small-batch low-latency config to compare.
[07:09] Dana Ortiz: will we need to provide admin creds for the infra, or is there an agent?
[07:13] Priya Rao: for Private installs we use a customer-managed control plane or we can run an agent that communicates outbound to your control endpoints; credentials are scoped and rotated.
[07:23] Marco Silva: fine, procurement wise we need an NDA then security docs. Liu and Aisha will coordinate requirements.
[07:30] Liu Chen: yes, once NDA is in place we'll share sanitized traffic.
[07:33] Aisha Rahman: also need a data flow diagram and encryption details.
[07:37] Jordan Kim: we'll send a kickoff packet with the pilot scope, security pack, and a sample contract redline.
[07:44] Priya Rao: quick technical note — because your workload has short-ish sequences mostly 512 tokens, prefix caching will help a lot; it reduces compute by reusing early token sequences. there's also a tradeoff: more caching means eventual consistency on model updates, but that's usually fine for scoring use cases.
[08:04] Marco Silva: good to know. any gotchas on quantization? we care about quality.
[08:09] Priya Rao: int8 can introduce small quality shifts, we can run evals on your prompt set and flag regressions; if needed we keep a mixed-precision path or fallback to a higher-precision variant for flagged prompts.
[08:20] Evan Park: we'll record the quality delta in the pilot report so you can make an informed cost/quality decision.
[08:27] Jordan Kim: ok let's cover next steps quickly.
[08:30] Marco Silva: sure.
[08:31] Jordan Kim: Actions: Jordan will send pilot scope + pricing; Priya will share benchmark plan; Redwood will send security pack; Tidal Bridge will provide sanitized workload once NDA is signed. schedule kickoff week of 2029-05-20. anything else?
[08:46] Aisha Rahman: can you also include an outline of the audit log schema and retention options?
[08:50] Priya Rao: yes we'll include that.
[08:52] Liu Chen: procurement will want a draft MSA; include termination/cost/commit language.
[08:56] Jordan Kim: will do.
[08:58] Marco Silva: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[09:01] Jordan Kim: thanks — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite.
[09:04] (meeting ends)

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts — product names like Redwood Dedicated transcribed as "Redwood dedicate" or "the dedicate pool"; network acronyms sometimes garbled (e.g., NAT recorded as 'natty'); speaker overlap once at ~06:20.

End of transcript.
